To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

excentric cleavages products of beta-caratone inhibit breast tumor cell proliferation and that these effects may be mediated through the down-regulation of cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor p21 and/or inhibition of the activator protein- 1 transcriptional factor.

the excentric cleave products of beta-carotenoid, beta-apo-carotenic acids, inhibit estrogen receptor-positive and estrogen receptor-negative breast tumor cell growth and that this effect may be mediated, in part, by the regulation of the E2F1/RB pathway and inhibition of AP- 1-mediated transcriptional activity.
excentric cleavages products of beta-carotenoids are potential chemopreventative agents for breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanisms of action of carotenoids in cancer prevention.
elucidating the molecular basis of the anti-tumorigenic effects of carotenoids.
the development of a chemopreventative strategy that would be based on the use of carotenoid cleavage products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
beta-apo-4'-CA and beta- apo-14'-CA have a significant effect on the proliferation of breast cancer cells in vitro.
beta-apo-carotenals inhibit breast tumor cell growth and that these effects may be mediated through the regulation of E2F-1 and/or RB proteins as well as inhibition of AP- 1 transcriptional activity.
the beta-apo-Ca compounds have a potential to become a new group of chemopreventives for breast cancer, but further research needs to be conducted to establish the efficacy of these compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the beta-apo-13'-CA, 14'-CA, 12'-CA, 10'-CA, 8'-CA, and the beta-apo-Carotenoic Acid Mixture (beta-apo-CAM), all inhibited MCF-10A cell growth in a dose-dependent fashion.
excentric cleavages of beta-carotenes are more effective than all-trans-retinoacids for the treatment of breast cancer.
beta-apo-CARs are potent inhibitors of breast tumor cells and that the mechanisms involved are not mediated by retinoid receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the beta-carotene cleavage products, beta-apo-carotenals, are more effective at inhibiting breast cancer cells than beta-carotene, and that beta-apo-carotenoic acid (beta-apo-CAs) is the most potent of these.
the excentric cleaved products of beta-carotenoid can inhibit the growth of breast cancer cells.
